answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut mandate and 14-day renewal deadline create immediate pressure, but the 94% assembly line utilization leaves no margin for supply disruption. Switching vendors (memory_c2) worked before but risks onboarding delays given the timeline. Deferring (memory_c5) is not viable with a hard expiration. Renewing (memory_c1) preserves stability but doesn't address the cost target. Adding a second source (memory_c3) would help risk but not the immediate cost reduction needed. Negotiating terms is the highest-leverage move: memory_c4 shows renegotiation recovered real margin against benchmarked market rates, and memory_c6 demonstrates the incumbent can move on pricing for volume/term commitment. Pulling memory_c4 to verify the negotiation playbook and benchmark approach will inform whether the incumbent has room to hit the 18% target. This preserves the option to escalate to vendor switch if negotiation fails, while keeping delivery risk low in the near term. The high utilization and short timeline mean we cannot afford the integration risk of a primary switch, but we can pressure the incumbent on price within their current relationship.
